M122R-01.title: Non-returncode OSError at three _mysql()-adjacent call sites crashes cleanup_run() uncaught instead of degrading to CLEANUP_FAIL
sites: diagnostics_snapshot() (invoked whenever out_dir is passed, i.e. every real qualification run)
M122R-01.consequence: Batch-aborting crash; for DROP-issuance and KILL specifically, the schema is left orphaned with zero rescue attempt because the crash occurs before the except VerificationError block that triggers rescue_cleanup().

M122R-02.title: Barrier candidate correlation is timing-based, not identity-based; rescue_cleanup() removes a surviving candidate unconditionally
M122R-02.evidence: core_findings_probe.json (s10), plus real qualification data: 3/20 and 3/20 (two independent full-battery runs) parallel runs observed non-empty candidate_barriers, both times self-resolved within one poll cycle with 0 rescue triggered
M122R-02.consequence: In principle (not observed in 40 real parallel-run samples across two independent batteries), a much slower sibling's still-active barrier could be seen as a surviving candidate at a run's own rescue phase, which would shutil.rmtree it -- rescue has no ownership check beyond 'is this path still there'.
